testName: Air Brakes Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: If the low air pressure warning signal comes on, what should you do?

options.text: Keep driving and have the brakes fixed within a week.
Pull over and check the brakes.
Call a mechanic while you are driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and check the brakes.
questions.explanation: If the low air pressure warning comes on, stop the vehicle safely while you can still control the brakes. Check and repair the brakes as soon as possible.

questions.question: What do air brakes use to work?
questions.explanation: Many large trucks use air brakes. Air brake systems use compressed air to operate.

questions.question: Which statement about emergency brakes is true?
questions.explanation: All trucks, truck tractors, and buses must have emergency brakes and parking brakes. These brakes work using mechanical force.

questions.question: When does the safety valve on the first air tank open?
questions.explanation: The safety valve on the first air tank opens when pressure gets too high, usually at 150 psi. If this valve opens, the brake system has a problem and needs to be repaired.

questions.question: How do you stop a vehicle with air brakes?

options.text: Pull out the air brake knob.

questions.explanation: To make a normal stop in a vehicle with air brakes, press the brake pedal down.

questions.question: What does an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) do?
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System prevents the wheels from locking up during hard braking. This gives you better control, but does not always make the vehicle stop in a shorter distance.

questions.question: How do you use the stab braking method?

options.text: Push the brakes all the way until the wheels lock, release until the wheels roll, then repeat.
Push the brakes halfway while keeping the wheels rolling.
Push the brakes all the way until the wheels lock and the vehicle stops.
Use the emergency brake until the vehicle slows down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push the brakes all the way until the wheels lock, release until the wheels roll, then repeat.
questions.explanation: The stab braking method means pushing the brakes all the way until they lock. Then release the brakes until the wheels start rolling again, and repeat this process.

questions.question: How do you apply the parking brake in a newer vehicle?
questions.explanation: In newer vehicles with air brakes, the parking brake uses a diamond-shaped yellow knob. Pull it out to apply the parking brake and push it in to release it.

questions.question: What color are ABS warning lights?
questions.explanation: Vehicles with Anti-Lock Braking Systems have yellow warning lights.

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with air brakes, check that ____ turn on automatically when air pressure drops below 45 psi.
questions.explanation: Before driving, check that spring brakes come on automatically when air pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi. Block the wheels and release air from the brake system by stepping on and off the brake pedal. When the pressure gets too low, the parking brake valve should pop out and spring brakes should come on.

questions.question: During a walk-around inspection, brake drums must not have cracks larger than ____ of the friction area width.
questions.explanation: Check the brake drums before each trip. Cracks larger than one half the friction area width are unsafe and mean you should not drive.

questions.question: What happens if brakes overheat?

options.text: The air compressor cools them down.

questions.explanation: Overheated brakes can stop working. This is called brake fade.

questions.question: Spring brakes activate when:

options.text: You turn on a dashboard control.

questions.explanation: Spring brakes turn on automatically when air pressure gets dangerously low. Exit the road safely and stop as soon as you see the low pressure warning.

questions.question: A modulating control valve controls the:
questions.explanation: A modulating control valve lets you apply spring brakes gradually. It is controlled by a lever on the dashboard.

questions.question: What must be on an air tank in an air-braked vehicle?
questions.explanation: All air tanks must have one-way check valves. They stop air from leaking out.

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with dual air brakes, at least ____ of pressure must build up in both brake systems.
questions.explanation: Let the air compressor build up at least 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems before driving.

questions.question: If the air pressure warning light comes on while driving, you should:

options.text: Turn on hazard lights and continue.
Safely exit the road and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Safely exit the road and stop.
questions.explanation: A warning light or buzzer means there is a problem with your air brake system. Stop and park safely right away.

questions.question: On newer vehicles, how do you set the parking brake?

options.text: Move a lever to the right.
Push in the yellow, diamond-shaped knob.
Pull out the yellow, diamond-shaped knob.
Pull up on the steering column.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull out the yellow, diamond-shaped knob.
questions.explanation: Pull the yellow, diamond-shaped knob out to set the parking brake. Push it in to release the brake.

questions.question: An air compressor governor stops pumping when air tanks reach:
questions.explanation: The governor stops the compressor at 125 psi. This is called the cut-out level.

questions.question: Air tank drains are used to:

options.text: Let rain water enter the tanks.
Remove water and oil from the tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove water and oil from the tanks.
questions.explanation: Air tanks have drains to remove water and oil. These liquids can damage the brakes if they build up in the system.

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with a dual air brake system, the air compressor must build at least ____ psi in both the primary and secondary systems.
questions.explanation: Before driving a vehicle with a dual air brake system, wait for the air compressor to build at least 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems.

questions.question: Air brakes are:

options.text: An effective way to stop large vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: An effective way to stop large vehicles.
questions.explanation: When properly maintained, air brakes are a safe and effective way to stop large, heavy vehicles.

questions.question: A tank endorsement is:

options.text: Needed to transport both liquids and gases.

questions.correctAnswerText: Needed to transport both liquids and gases.
questions.explanation: A tank endorsement is required to drive a tank vehicle that carries either liquids or gases.

questions.question: Most heavy-duty vehicles use:
questions.explanation: Most heavy-duty vehicles use dual air brake systems. These have two separate braking systems controlled by one set of controls. Each system operates brakes on different axles.

questions.question: If air tanks have manually operated drains, how often should you drain them?
questions.explanation: In an air brake system with manually operated drains, drain the tanks at the end of each driving day.
